repomix.files: This section contains the contents of the repository's files. 1: --- 2: name: deploying-to-cloud 3: description: "Deploys and manages Laravel applications on Laravel Cloud using the `cloud` CLI. Use when the user wants to deploy an app, ship to Cloud, create or manage applications, environments, databases, caches, object storage, queues, domains, instances, background processes, secrets, compute, scheduled tasks, or Laravel Cloud infrastructure; or check billing, usage, or spend. Triggers on deployment, shipping, Cloud management, environment setup, database provisioning, billing or usage queries, the `cloud` CLI, and Laravel Cloud deployment troubleshooting." 4: license: MIT 5: metadata: 6: author: laravel 7: --- 8: 9: # Deploying with Laravel Cloud 10: 11: Use the [Laravel Cloud documentation](https://cloud.laravel.com/docs/llms.txt) for detailed, current feature behavior. Use the Cloud CLI for Cloud operations rather than guessing dashboard or API workflows. Install it in the project and invoke it as `./vendor/bin/cloud` by default; use a globally installed `cloud` command only as a fallback. Commands below are written as `cloud` for brevity; run them as `./vendor/bin/cloud` unless falling back to the global installation. 12: 13: ## Application Setup 14: 15: - Laravel Cloud deploys from GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket. A new Laravel application requires PHP 8.2 or later, Laravel 9 or later, a connected Git provider, and a deployment region. 16: - Cloud creates environments for applications. Use separate production, staging, and preview environments; each environment has its own compute, resources, and deployment settings. 17: - Keep application compute and attached resources in the same region where possible. 18: - Cloud builds a Docker image using the selected PHP version, runs the configured build and deploy commands, and switches traffic to a successful deployment with zero downtime. Push-to-deploy is enabled by default, and manual deployments and deploy hooks are also available. 19: 20: ## Build and Deploy 21: 22: - A typical Laravel build command is `composer install --no-dev && npm run build`. 23: - Run optimization and cache-building commands during the build, not during deployment. A typical deploy command is `php artisan migrate --force`. 24: - Build and deploy commands have a 15-minute timeout. Deploy commands run immediately before the release becomes live, and filesystem changes made by deploy commands are not persisted. 25: - Do not add `php artisan queue:restart`, `php artisan horizon:terminate`, `php artisan optimize:clear`, or `php artisan storage:link` to deploy commands. Cloud handles worker restarts and process management; deploy filesystem changes are not persistent. 26: - After changing environment settings, attached resources, or linked secrets, redeploy the environment for the changes to take effect. 27: 28: ## Configuration and Resources 29: 30: - Attached databases, caches, and object storage inject their connection variables automatically. Custom environment variables take precedence over injected values. 31: - Use Secrets Manager for encrypted organization-level values shared across environments. Secret values cannot be read after creation; redeploy affected environments after creating, updating, linking, unlinking, or deleting a secret. 32: - Environment filesystems are ephemeral and are not shared between replicas. Use a database or Laravel Valkey for persistent cache and sessions, and Laravel Cloud Object Storage for persistent files. Do not rely on local files surviving a deployment. 33: 34: ### Object Storage and File Visibility 35: 36: - Laravel Cloud Object Storage is backed by Cloudflare R2. R2 applies visibility at the bucket level; a bucket cannot contain a mix of private and public objects. 37: - For private files, always use `Storage::disk()` with no arguments, such as `Storage::disk()->put(...)`, so Laravel uses the environment's default disk. Do not pass a disk name for private/default storage. Attach a private Cloud bucket as the environment's default disk. 38: - For public files, use the named public disk: `Storage::disk('public')->put(...)`. Attach a second Cloud bucket configured as public and give it the `public` disk name. 39: - Applications that use both private and public files therefore need two Cloud Object Storage buckets attached to the environment: a private default bucket and a public bucket named `public`. 40: - Do not set per-file or Flysystem `visibility: 'public'` configuration for Cloud Object Storage. R2 does not support per-object ACL headers and rejects those requests; select the bucket visibility when creating the bucket. 41: - Private buckets are not internet-accessible, but Laravel can generate temporary public URLs with `Storage::temporaryUrl(...)`. Public buckets expose all objects through their Cloud-provided public URL. 42: - Install the S3 Flysystem adapter before using Cloud Object Storage: `composer require league/flysystem-aws-s3-v3 "^3.0" --with-all-dependencies`. 43: 44: ## Queues and Scheduling 45: 46: - Managed queues are the recommended queue option. They provision dedicated workers and autoscale based on queued work. 47: - Managed queues require a supported recent Laravel version and `aws/aws-sdk-php`; check the current Cloud documentation before changing dependencies. 48: - Enable the scheduler on an App or Worker cluster to run `php artisan schedule:run` every minute. When an environment has multiple replicas, use Laravel's `onOneServer` for tasks that must run once. 49: - Only Flex compute sizes can scale to zero. Scale-to-zero environments wake for Laravel scheduled tasks and queued jobs, but long-running jobs may be interrupted when the sleep timeout is reached. Use managed queues for workloads that must not be interrupted. 50: 51: ## Domains and Storage 52: 53: - Each environment receives a `laravel.cloud` domain after its first successful deployment. Cloud automatically verifies custom domains and provisions SSL after the required DNS records are configured. 54: - Do not use the ephemeral filesystem for persistent uploads, generated files, cache, or session data. Use the appropriate Cloud resource instead. 55: 56: ## Cloud CLI 57: 58: ### Setup 59: 60: ```shell 61: composer require --dev laravel/cloud-cli 62: ./vendor/bin/cloud auth -n 63: ``` 64: 65: If a project-local installation is not available, install the CLI globally with `composer global require laravel/cloud-cli` and invoke it as `cloud`. 66: 67: `cloud auth` opens a browser. If a browser is unavailable, set `LARAVEL_CLOUD_TOKEN` in the environment. It overrides any saved token and writes nothing to disk. To save a token instead, run `cloud auth:token --add --token=<token> -n` or pipe it with `echo "$TOKEN" | cloud auth:token --add -n`. 68: 69: ### Commands 70: 71: Commands follow a CRUD pattern: `resource:list`, `resource:get`, `resource:create`, `resource:update`, `resource:delete`. 72: 73: Available resources: `application`, `environment`, `instance`, `database-cluster`, `database`, `cache`, `bucket`, `domain`, `websocket-cluster`, `background-process`, `secret`, `command`, `deployment`. 74: 75: Some resources have additional commands (e.g., `domain:verify`, `database:open`, `instance:sizes`, `cache:types`, `<resource>:metrics`). Discover these via `cloud -h`. 76: 77: Never hardcode command signatures. Always run `cloud <command> -h` to discover options at runtime. 78: 79: ### CLI Flags 80: 81: - Always add `-n` to every command to prevent the CLI from hanging. 82: - Never use `-q` or `--silent`; they suppress all output. 83: 84: Flag combos per operation: 85: - Read (`:list`, `:get`) → `--json -n` 86: - Create (`:create`) → `--json -n` 87: - Update (`:update`) → `--json -n --force` 88: - Delete (`:delete`) → `-n --force` (no `--json`) 89: - Environment variables → `-n --force` 90: - Deploy or ship → `-n` with all options passed explicitly (no `--json`) 91: 92: ### Deployment Workflow 93: 94: Determine the task and follow the matching path: 95: 96: - First deployment: inspect `cloud ship -h`, then run `cloud ship -n` with all required values. 97: 98: - Existing application: 99: ```shell 100: cloud deploy {app_name} {environment} -n --open 101: cloud deploy:monitor -n 102: ``` 103: 104: - Environment variables: `cloud environment:variables -n --force` 105: 106: - Secrets: `echo "$VALUE" | cloud secret:create --name=NAME --json -n`, then `cloud environment-secret:attach` 107: 108: - Provision infrastructure: `cloud <resource>:create --json -n` 109: 110: - Monorepo (application in a subdirectory): add `--root-directory=<subdir>` to `cloud ship` or `cloud application:create`. 111: 112: - Custom domain: `cloud domain:create --json -n`, then `cloud domain:verify -n`. 113: 114: - Repository defaults: `cloud repo:config {application} -n` sets repository-local application and organization defaults. Pass `--organization=<id|name|slug>` when the user has multiple organizations. 115: 116: For multi-step operations, see [reference/checklists.md](reference/checklists.md). 117: 118: - If the user's needs are unclear, ask before running anything. 119: 120: ### When a Command Fails 121: 122: 1. Read the error output. 123: 2. Check the resource status with `:list --json -n` or `:get --json -n`. 124: 3. For authentication errors, run `cloud auth -n`. 125: 4. Fix the issue and rerun the command. 126: 5. If the same error occurs after one fix, stop and ask the user rather than repeating the operation. 127: 128: Always run `cloud deploy:monitor -n` after every deploy. If it fails, inspect the deployment status and logs and show the user what went wrong before attempting a fix. 129: 130: ### Subagent Delegation 131: 132: Delegate high-output operations to subagents using the Task tool to keep the main context window small. Only the summary returns; verbose output stays in the subagent's context. 133: 134: Delegate these to a subagent: 135: - `cloud deploy:monitor -n` — deployment logs can be very long 136: - `cloud deployment:get --json -n` — full deployment details 137: - `cloud <resource>:list --json -n` — listing many resources produces large JSON 138: - `cloud <resource>:metrics --json -n` — every data point is included; narrow it with `--fields` (e.g. `--fields=period,cpuUsage.average`) 139: - `cloud command:run` — when output may be long 140: - `cloud usage --detailed --json -n` — the payload includes details for every database, cache, bucket, websocket, and application 141: - Fetching docs from https://cloud.laravel.com/docs/llms.txt via `WebFetch` 142: 143: Keep in the main context: 144: - Short commands like `:create`, `:delete`, `:update` — output is small 145: - `cloud deploy -n` — you need the deployment ID immediately 146: - Any command where you need the result for the next step right away 147: 148: ### Rules 149: 150: Follow these rules: 151: - Flag selection — always use the documented combos above 152: - Deploy sequence — deploy then monitor, never skip monitoring 153: - Destructive commands — always confirm with the user first, show the command and wait for approval. This includes deleting applications, environments, databases, caches, buckets, domains, or secrets. 154: - Error loop — diagnose, fix once, ask user if it fails again 155: 156: Use judgment for: 157: - Instance sizes, regions, cluster types — ask the user if not specified 158: - Which resources to provision — based on what the user describes 159: - Order of provisioning — no strict sequence required 160: - How to present output — summarize, show raw, or extract fields based on context 161: 162: ### Secrets 163: 164: Secrets are encrypted values shared across the organization and attached to environments. The CLI encrypts values locally, so plaintext never reaches the API. 165: 166: ```shell 167: cloud secret:list --json -n 168: echo "$VALUE" | cloud secret:create --name=STRIPE_KEY --json -n 169: cloud environment-secret:attach {environment} {secretId} -n 170: cloud environment-secret:list {environment} --json -n 171: ``` 172: 173: Pipe the value in. `--value=` works, but leaves the plaintext in shell history and the process list. 174: 175: `secret:update`, `secret:delete`, and `environment-secret:attach` take secret IDs, not names — names are not unique. Read IDs from `cloud secret:list --json -n`. 176: 177: There is no `secret:get`, and no way to detach a secret from a single environment. `secret:delete` removes it and detaches it everywhere. 178: 179: Secrets need the `sodium` PHP extension. No other command does. 180: 181: Redeploy affected environments after creating, updating, attaching, or deleting a secret. 182: 183: ### Remote Access 184: 185: #### Tinker (v0.2.0 or later) 186: 187: Run PHP code directly in a Cloud environment: 188: 189: ```shell 190: cloud tinker {environment} --code='Your PHP code here' --timeout=60 -n 191: ``` 192: 193: - `--code` — PHP code to execute (required in non-interactive mode) 194: - `--timeout` — maximum number of seconds to wait for output (default: 60) 195: 196: The code must explicitly output results using `echo`, `dump`, or similar; expressions alone produce no output. 197: 198: Always pass `--code` and `-n` to avoid interactive prompts. 199: 200: #### Remote Commands 201: 202: Run shell commands on a Cloud environment: 203: 204: ```shell 205: cloud command:run {environment} --cmd='your command here' -n 206: ``` 207: 208: - `--cmd` — the command to run (required in non-interactive mode) 209: - `--no-monitor` — skip real-time output streaming 210: - `--copy-output` — copy output to clipboard 211: 212: Review past commands: 213: 214: - `cloud command:list {environment} --json -n` — list command history 215: - `cloud command:get {commandId} --json -n` — get details and output of a specific command 216: 217: ### Billing and Usage 218: 219: View billing and usage for the current organization: 220: 221: ```shell 222: cloud usage --json -n 223: ``` 224: 225: - `--period=current|previous|1|2|3` — Billing period (default: `current`; `1`, `2`, and `3` are one, two, and three periods back, respectively). Other values return an error. 226: - `--environment=<id>` — filter usage to a single environment 227: - `--detailed` — include per-application, per-resource, and per-add-on breakdowns 228: - `--json` — machine-readable output (always pair with `-n`) 229: 230: Common queries: 231: 232: - Current spend: `cloud usage --json -n | jq '.currentSpendCents'` 233: - Last month's bill: `cloud usage --period=previous --json -n` 234: - One environment, full breakdown: `cloud usage --environment=<id> --detailed --json -n` 235: 236: All amounts are in cents. Keys are camelCase at every level (e.g., `currentSpendCents`, `bandwidth.allowanceBytes`, `databases[].totalCents`, `applications[].totalCostCents`). 237: 238: ### Config 239: 240: 1. Environment: `LARAVEL_CLOUD_TOKEN` — an API token, taking precedence over any saved one (empty counts as unset) 241: 2. Global: `~/.config/cloud/config.json` — auth tokens and preferences 242: 3. Repo-local: `.cloud/config.json` — app and environment defaults (set by `cloud repo:config {application} -n`) 243: 4. CLI arguments override both config files 244: 245: Pass the application to `repo:config`. Without it, the command must prompt and fails under `-n` when the organization has more than one application. Deploy commands do not need these defaults; pass the application and environment to them directly. 246: 247: Using multiple organizations requires multiple stored API tokens. Commands read `organization_id` from `.cloud/config.json` to select one and fail if it is not set. Set it with `cloud repo:config {application} --organization=<id|name|slug> -n`. 248: 249: `LARAVEL_CLOUD_TOKEN` holds one token, so it picks the organization on its own. Naming a different one with `--organization` fails rather than falling back to the token's organization. 250: 251: ## Documentation 252: 253: Laravel Cloud documentation: https://cloud.laravel.com/docs/llms.txt 254: 255: When the user asks how something works or needs an explanation of a Laravel Cloud feature, fetch the docs from the URL above using `WebFetch` and use it to provide accurate answers. 256: 257: ## When Stuck 258: 259: - Fetch https://cloud.laravel.com/docs/llms.txt for official documentation 260: - Run `cloud <command> -h` for any command's options 261: - Run `cloud -h` to discover commands 262: 263: ## Verification 264: 265: 1. Confirm the target application and environment before changing or deploying anything. 266: 2. Check staged environment changes and required resources before deployment. 267: 3. Monitor every deployment to completion with `cloud deploy:monitor -n`. 268: 4. For production changes, verify the application URL, logs, queues, scheduled tasks, and relevant resource health. 1: <?php 2: 3: declare(strict_types=1); 4: 5: namespace App\Console\Commands; 6: 7: use Illuminate\Console\Command; 8: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB; 9: use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage; 10: use Throwable; 11: 12: /** 13: * F13: afterRollBack cleanup never runs when the process itself dies 14: * (max_execution_time, OOM, worker restart) — the DB rolls back on 15: * disconnect but the orphaned R2 files stay. Laravel. اختبارات المتصفح تستخدم استجابات مطابقة لهذا العقد؛ لا تدّعي اختبار حساب R2 خارجي أو صلاحيات حساب إنتاج. 8: 9: كل المسارات التالية تحت `/api/v1/admin` وتتطلب جلسة المستخدم وصلاحيات العملية. 10: 11: | المسار | الطلب والرد | 12: | --- | --- | 13: | GET /categories?tree=1 | `{data:[...]}`؛ كل قسم يتضمن `parent_id`, `is_active`, `children` | 14: | GET /brands | بحث، حالة، pagination؛ `{data:Brand}` | 17: | POST /brands/{id} | multipart مع `_method=PUT`؛ `remove_logo=1` للإزالة | 18: | DELETE /brands/{id} | `{message}`؛ 422 عند الارتباط بمنتجات، بما فيها المحذوفة | 19: | GET /products | `{data,links,meta}`؛ كل الفلاتر في URL، والإحصاءات بطلبات مستقلة غير مفلترة | 20: | GET /products/{id} | `{data:Product}`؛ `dimensions` متداخلة، وcategory وbrand وvariants | 21: | POST `{message,errors}`. رفض النشر يحتوي `errors.status` كمصفوفة نصوص؛ أخطاء المتغير الفردي تأتي بدون prefix. 34: 35: ## نتيجة مراجعة المراحل 36: 37: | المرحلة | التنفيذ | 38: | --- | --- | 39: | 0 | فحص التكامل 52: 53: - ترتيب `name` في API بحسب الاسم الإنجليزي؛ الواجهة تسميه «الاسم (EN)». 54: - صورة اللون تُربط بأول متغير محفوظ لهذا اللون بحسب ترتيب الصفوف، وتُجمع عند القراءة باسم اللون الإنجليزي. حذف المتغير يحذف صوره؛ حوار الحذف ينبه لذلك. هذا هو عقد الإدارة المعتمد هنا، ويجب أن يستهلكه المتجر بنفس المعنى. 55: - رفع الملفات يمر عبر backend الحالي الذي يخزنها على R2؛ الواجهة لا تحتوي مفاتيح تخزين. معاينات الملفات المحلية مؤقتة وتُلغى عند انتهاء عرضها. 56: - اختيار المورد يظل معطلاً كما في التصميم لأن قائمة الموردين غير مجهزة بهذه الشاشة؛ قيمة المورد المحفوظة تُحفظ عند التعديل. 57: - استخدمت اختبارات Laravel المعزولة بدلاً من إعادة تشغيل Seeder على قاعدة المستخدم. لم تُمسح أو تُعد تهيئة قاعدة البيانات. 58: 59: ## التحقق 60: 61: - Laravel Catalog: **119 اختباراً، 542 assertion البراندات ورفض حذفها، 404، العرض فقط، والموبايل. 64: - `pnpm --filter @alfarid/backoffice build` يجمع TypeScript ونسخة الإنتاج. 1: # مراجعة تنفيذ branch.txt 2: 3: تاريخ التحقق: 23 أكتوبر 2026. 4: 5:
